Give your AI a Google Ads campaign export and it tells you which Search campaigns change in February.

Google Ads now lets you rank channels and cap the low priority ones at a share of daily budget. Our view is that most brands should swap their search partner and Display opt-outs for low priority with a small cap. An opt-out tells you nothing. A 5% cap tells you something after a month.

From February 2027, every Search campaign with Display Expansion on moves onto these settings anyway.

Give your AI a campaign export with the Display setting, bid strategy and budget status, and it gives you back a table of which campaigns migrate and a suggested Display setting for each. The decision stays with you.

The full episode and article are at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/google-ads-channel-prioritisation-paid-teams/ (the podcast voices are AI-generated).
clips.text: Our view, and it's in the article, is that most brands should swap their search partner and Display opt-outs for low priority with a small cap. An opt-out tells you nothing. A five per cent cap tells you something after a month. And Google's announcement speaks directly to people who've historically opted out. Until now those teams had no way to try either network at a cost they controlled. For a cycling or endurance retailer, I'd do that in late October on a budget-limited bikes or kit campaign. Four weeks of evidence before Black Friday, and if it doesn't earn its place you've lost very little.

From February 2027, every Google Ads Search campaign with Display Expansion on migrates to channel prioritisation automatically, and Display stops serving on campaigns that use Target Impression Share. If you run several accounts, that is a lot of clicking.

Give your AI a campaign export with the Display setting, bid strategy and budget status. It gives you back a table of which campaigns migrate, which use Target Impression Share, and a suggested Display setting for each. 50% where Display is earning its keep, a lower cap where nobody has checked.

You still make the call on each campaign. You just make it from a list.

The prompt is in the show notes, with the full episode and article at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/google-ads-channel-prioritisation-paid-teams/ (the podcast voices are AI-generated).
clips.text: Get AI on this. First job, the February audit. Every Search campaign with Display switched on, and what happens to each one. Give your AI a campaign export from Google Ads with the Display setting, bid strategy and budget status, and it gives you back a table. Which campaigns migrate, which use Target Impression Share, and a suggested Display setting for each, fifty per cent where Display's earning its keep and a lower cap where nobody's checked. The decision on each one stays with you. But you're deciding from a list instead of clicking through accounts.
